YOUR DATA, EXPLAINED.

Privacy Policy

Your Google Drive belongs to you. This policy explains what Cloudlane accesses, where it is stored, and how you can remove it.

Publisher: bdn236Effective: 17 October 2026Last updated: 17 October 2026

The essential facts: Cloudlane connects your Windows PC directly to Google Drive. The publisher does not operate a server that receives your Drive files or account tokens. The app stores sign-in tokens locally, and its optional media cache stores downloaded content on your PC.

1. Who this policy covers

Cloudlane is independently published by bdn236 (the “publisher,” “we,” or “us”). This policy covers the Cloudlane website and the Windows app distributed from it. Google, the website host, and other apps you use have their own policies.

2. Google Drive access

Sign-in takes place in your browser on Google's authorization pages. Cloudlane receives authorization tokens after you approve access; it does not receive your Google password.

The app requests https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive, which permits viewing and managing your Drive files. It uses this access to provide the drive you connect in Windows Explorer, including browsing existing folders, streaming and opening files, uploading, creating folders, renaming, and moving deleted items to Google Drive Trash.

To provide those features, the app processes:

  • Your Google account email address, display name and an account identifier, to distinguish connected accounts.
  • File and folder metadata, such as names, IDs, sizes, types, timestamps, parent folders and permissions relevant to the requested operation.
  • Your storage quota and usage, to display drive capacity.
  • File content when it is requested for an upload, download, streaming operation or local media cache. Windows Explorer and apps you open files with may also request content.

You choose which accounts to connect. Connecting an account does not transfer ownership of its files to the publisher.

3. What stays on your PC

  • Sign-in tokens: access and refresh tokens are saved in local account files protected using Windows Data Protection for the Windows user who saved them.
  • Settings: account email addresses, account identifiers, drive names and letters, startup preferences and cache settings are stored locally. Some settings are ordinary local JSON rather than encrypted token files.
  • Upload references: pending-upload information can include the original local file path, target folder, progress and upload-session information. Cloudlane encrypts persisted upload references; direct uploads read the original file without making a separate full payload copy for uploading.
  • Optional media cache: downloaded image/video content and cache metadata are stored on a local disk, with a rolling shared limit of about 2 GiB. This cache is not encrypted by Cloudlane. Other apps may create their own caches or copies.
  • Diagnostics: local diagnostic information can include timings, request status and file or path details. The app does not automatically send diagnostics to the publisher. Review information before choosing to share it.

4. Use and sharing

Google account and Drive data are used to perform the user-facing features described above. They are not sold, used for advertising, supplied to data brokers, or used to train general-purpose AI models.

Drive requests travel between your PC and Google over HTTPS. Files you open or copy can be accessed by the Windows applications or destinations you choose. Cloudlane's local Explorer connection also makes the mounted files available to software running with the relevant access on your PC.

Cloudlane follows the Google API Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements. The publisher does not routinely receive or review your Drive content. If you voluntarily email support or send diagnostics, we receive what you choose to send and use it to address your request, maintain security, or meet applicable legal requirements. Do not send passwords, tokens, or unnecessary file content.

5. Website and other providers

The website provides product information and an installer download. It does not connect to your Drive, offer a Cloudlane account database, include advertising trackers or analytics, or collect email addresses through forms.

The site is hosted on Netlify. Hosting providers may process connection information, such as IP addresses, requested URLs, browser information and timestamps, for delivery, security and operational logs. The site loads its DM Sans typeface from Google Fonts, whose servers receive connection information when that font is requested. The pages do not set advertising cookies.

Google processes your use of Google services under its Privacy Policy. Support messages sent to support@hisabi.store are handled through the publisher's email service. Providers apply their own retention and processing practices.

6. Retention and removal

Local tokens and settings remain until you remove them. Cached media can be evicted as the cache fills, but disabling caching or uninstalling the app should not be treated as secure deletion of existing content.

  1. Stop access: disconnect the drive or exit Cloudlane to stop its active connections. In Google Account connections, remove Cloudlane's access to revoke the authorization.
  2. Remove a local account: disconnect that account, then use Forget account. This removes its local account selection and attempts to delete its saved sign-in token. It does not revoke Google's authorization or erase retained upload references and media cache.
  3. Clear media: disconnect all Cloudlane drives and use Clear cache. Check the selected cache folder if you want to remove any remaining copies.
  4. Remove all app data: exit Cloudlane, then remove its data-direct folder beside the installed executable and any separately selected media-cache folder. This removes local preferences, sign-ins and pending-upload references; pending work may be lost. Uninstalling the app retains this user data by design.

Removing local Cloudlane data does not delete your Google Drive files. File operations you explicitly perform through a connected drive, including deletion to Trash, can change those cloud files. Copies opened or saved using other software are governed by that software.

If you contact support, messages may be kept while addressing the request and for necessary follow-up, security or legal obligations. You can ask the publisher about access, correction or deletion of support information. We cannot erase data controlled independently by Google or another provider.

7. Security

Cloudlane uses browser-based OAuth with PKCE, HTTPS for Google API requests, and Windows user encryption for persisted sign-in tokens. These measures do not guarantee absolute security. Software with access to your Windows session may be able to access mounted files or local account data. Protect your PC and use operating-system disk encryption where appropriate, especially for cached media.

The public Desktop OAuth registration embedded in the app identifies Cloudlane. It is separate from your personal account tokens and does not itself grant access to your Drive.

8. Policy changes

Changes will be published on this page with an updated date. Material changes to how Google user data is accessed, used or shared will be disclosed before the changed processing begins, with additional consent where required.
